title: Directly imported dependencies must be declared in requirements/skinny-requirements.yaml and propagated to the derived pyproject files and uv.lock
answers: mlflow-skinny dependency not declared but imported directly
how do I add a runtime dependency to mlflow skinny
why does pip install mlflow pick a broken transitive package version
where do I put an anyio or other transitive package constraint
body:
Invariant: a package that mlflow imports directly must be declared in requirements/skinny-requirements.yaml, not left to arrive transitively via starlette or another dependency.
Enforced at: requirements/skinny-requirements.yaml (per-package block with pip_release, minimum, max_major_version, unsupported), which generates the dependencies list in pyproject.toml and libs/skinny/pyproject.toml, and the resolved entries in uv.lock.
What breaks if skipped: an undeclared package can be upgraded by any transitive resolver to a release that breaks mlflow at import or request time. A pin in uv.lock does not protect users who run pip install mlflow, because pip resolves live from PyPI and reads only the published mlflow-skinny metadata.
Constraints: edit the YAML and regenerate the derived files rather than hand-editing pyproject.toml. Put exclusions of known-broken releases in the YAML unsupported list so the != specifier reaches the published metadata. Keep the lockfile churn to the affected package.
applies: Any change to the runtime dependency set of mlflow or mlflow-skinny.
says: Installing the client package pulls an incompatible dependency that crashes at startup.
Fresh installation fails during server requests because an underlying dependency is broken.
The application crashes on import after installing because a direct dependency was omitted.
Ensure package installations exclude known broken third party library releases automatically.
Why does installing the lightweight package fail when indirect dependencies get upgraded?
search: Every package directly imported by mlflow must be explicitly declared in requirements/skinny-requirements.yaml rather than relying on transitive dependencies from libraries like starlette. Declarations in requirements/skinny-requirements.yaml configure pip_release, minimum, max_major_version, and unsupported lists to generate dependencies in pyproject.toml, libs/skinny/pyproject.toml, and uv.lock. Developers must modify the YAML file and regenerate derived files instead of hand-editing pyproject.toml, ensuring known-broken package releases are placed in the unsupported list so != specifiers reach published metadata. This rule applies to any runtime dependency change for mlflow or mlflow-skinny, protecting pip install users where lockfile pins do not govern live PyPI resolution.
